title: Let Every Creature Join
description: Let Every Creature Join in Tonic Solfa to FRANCONIA, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 16 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 148, part 3, headed “Universal praise”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to FRANCONIA; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Let ev-ery crea-ture join To praise th'e-ter-nal God; Ye heav-enly hosts, the song be-gin, And sound his Name a-broad.

lines: Ye heavenly hosts, the song begin,
Ye starry lights, ye twinkling flames,
By his command they stand or move,
Or fall in showers, or snow,
Ye thunders, murmuring round the skies,
When ye in dreadful storms conspire
But saints that taste his saving love
Praise him, ye watery worlds below,
From humble shrubs and cedars high,
Ye live upon his daily food,
Or sit on flowery boughs, and sing
And flies, in all your shining swarms,
Praise him that drest you so.
But saints that know his heavenly grace
Should learn to praise him best.
While growing babes, and withering age,
God is the Lord: his name alone
But saints that dwell so near his heart,

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to FRANCONIA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
